damage_classes.name: Structural Shear / Diagonal Crack
damage_classes.risk_description: Diagonal cracking in beams/columns indicates principal tensile stress exceeding concrete shear capacity. Immediate shoring required.
damage_classes.recommended_treatment: Low-viscosity epoxy resin injection under 0.2-0.4 MPa pressure followed by carbon fiber (CFRP) wrapping.

damage_classes.name: Spalling with Exposed Corroded Rebar
damage_classes.risk_description: Carbonation or chloride ingress has depassivated reinforcing steel, leading to volumetric expansion (rust) popping off concrete cover.
damage_classes.recommended_treatment: Chipping loose concrete, sandblasting rebar, zinc-rich anti-corrosion primer coating, polymer-modified structural mortar (PMM) rebuilding.

damage_classes.name: Severe Moisture Ingress & Efflorescence
damage_classes.risk_description: Hydrostatic pressure causing dampness, leaching calcium hydroxide crystals, deteriorating internal plaster and embedded conduit lines.
damage_classes.recommended_treatment: Negative-side crystalline waterproofing slurry coat + polyurethane (PU) flexible injection grouting.

damage_classes.name: Honeycombing / Consolidation Voids
damage_classes.risk_description: Poor compaction during casting leaving coarse aggregate pockets with zero cement matrix, drastically diminishing compressive strength.
damage_classes.recommended_treatment: Pressure grouting with non-shrink high-strength micro-concrete (M60 grade).

damage_classes.name: Plastic Shrinkage Hairline Cracks (<0.3mm)
damage_classes.risk_description: Early-age thermal or moisture shrinkage cracks confined to surface layer. No immediate structural danger but allows moisture ingress if unsealed.
damage_classes.recommended_treatment: Elastomeric acrylic micro-crack sealer and protective anti-carbonation topcoat.
